text:
**Verdict: False as commonly meant.** From low Earth orbit, the Great Wall is not reliably distinguishable to the unaided eye: it is narrow and blends into the surrounding terrain. NASA Earth Observatory’s discussion of astronaut imagery describes it as difficult to see from orbit.

The wording needs a caveat: “space” covers many distances, and cameras or zoom can reveal sections. So it is not impossible to photograph from orbit, but the usual claim that it stands out to the naked eye is misleading.
